title: Secret-value handling and test support
cluster_summary: Root cause: WhatGroup's Compat.GetSpellCooldownRemaining does a comparison and arithmetic on GetSpellCooldown's startTime and duration, which can be secret in combat, and it never checks the plain isActive 5th return that LibKa0s Compat's contract tells callers to decide with. The real fix is local to WhatGroup (WG-R-01). It should not return 0 ('ready') when the values are secret. It should decide on isActive and return an 'unknown' signal so the ticker stays armed. Support work: LibKa0s adds an additive testkit secret simulator (WG-R-09) first, and WhatGroup's regression tests then use that simulator after re-vendoring (WG-R-02). The standard's §8 named list gets a hygiene addition (WG-R-08). The finding's claim that audits downgrade this class is wrong, because §8 already has a catch-all and the defect is a comparison, not pre-formatting. MultiMeters' diagnostics-only isLocalPlayer compare (MM-R-07) is optional and should be folded into its F-006 PlainTruth export.

verdicts.assessment: Verified at WhatGroup/core/Compat.lua:110-114: `start <= 0 or duration <= GCD_SECONDS` and `(start + duration) - GetTime()` run on values that LibKa0s Compat.lua:232-233 says may be secret, with no IsSecret guard. A raise kills the AceTimer ticker and aborts ShowNotification before ShowFrame. Severity is medium because no one has confirmed in the client that a teleport cooldown is secret, and the bug needs a join that happens in combat (smoke S-001). The proposed '0,false when secret' would report a teleport that is on cooldown as READY, so it is corrected.
verdicts.remediation: In Compat.GetSpellCooldownRemaining, also take the 5th return isActive. When start or duration is secret (Compat.IsSecret: the library's IsSecret, or the 3-line issecretvalue stub when the library is absent), do no arithmetic. Return an 'unknown' signal (for example nil plus isActive) and do not return 0. Have the chat Teleport row and the popup button decide 'on cooldown' from isActive. Have the Frame.lua ticker keep its last text and stay armed on an unknown tick. Add one-line notes to docs/compat-layer.md and module-map.md in the same commit. The owner runs smoke S-001.

verdicts.assessment: WhatGroup/tests/wow_mock.lua:568-571 returns only plain numbers, and no test defines issecretvalue, so a regression to WG-R-01 would pass all cases. The regression tests are worth adding. They should be built on the kit simulator from WG-R-09, not on a local mock that would have to be retired later.
verdicts.remediation: After WG-R-09 lands and tests/_kit is re-vendored, add red-under cases built on the kit's secret helper. Required: the compat compare and the ticker surviving a secret tick. Optional: the notify path. The mocked cooldown table must make startTime and duration secret while isActive stays plain. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit as the repo gate requires. Write a local mock.secret only if WG-R-09 is deferred.

verdicts.assessment: The §8 named list (events-frames-taint.md:163-172) does omit C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown, and the standard's own maintenance rule says to extend it. But the list already has an 'any other API a client build protects' catch-all, and it scopes the pre-formatting rule, while F-001 is a comparison defect that the §8 'never compare' MUST NOT already covers. So the claim that audits downgraded F-001 is refuted, and this is documentation hygiene.
verdicts.remediation: Add C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown startTime/duration/modRate to the §8 named list and spell cooldowns to the §8 intro examples. Also add C_Spell.GetSpellCooldownDuration's :GetRemainingDuration(), which KickCD/docs/compat-layer.md:19 documents as secret in combat. Make a patch-level standard version bump with a changelog entry. Per-addon re-vendoring of the standard can wait for the routine sweep.

verdicts.assessment: LibKa0s/testkit has no secret support. Hand-rolled secret mocks exist in about 7 consumers (AuraMaster, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, MultiMeters, Outfitter, PFE, plus LibKa0s's own tests). The real case is duplication and reuse, not an anti-pattern #47 violation (#47 names whole harnesses and toolkits). Anti-pattern #55 argues against forcing divergent consumer semantics into the kit.
verdicts.remediation: Add an additive Kit.secret(v) to LibKa0s testkit that raises on compare, arithmetic, concat and boolean test, plus an issecretvalue installer the mocks answer. Bump Kit.VERSION and re-vendor tests/_kit into consumers as its own commit through the normal re-vendor step. Do not migrate existing local mocks in this run (MultiMeters' mock_secrets.lua models more). Only WhatGroup (WG-R-02) adopts it now, and migrations are optional follow-ups.

verdicts.assessment: Provider.lua:551/:649 compare isLocalPlayer unguarded, and the noteValue short-circuit `type(value)=="boolean" or ...` at :676 would let a secret boolean through to tostring and table keying. But the code runs only for diagnostics, the probes are pcall-wrapped, and isLocalPlayer is documented as plain today, so the worst case is one lost diagnostics section. PlainTruth is still file-local in Aggregator.lua:446.
verdicts.remediation: Fold this into the F-006 commit if F-006 exports PlainTruth from core/Secrets.lua: route both isLocalPlayer probes through it, and in noteValue gate on `not Secrets.IsSecret(value)` before the boolean short-circuit. If F-006 is declined, make only the noteValue reorder (or route through Secrets.CanAccess). Do not open a standalone item.
